GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: On 2026-11-09, 159 scoped existing frontend tests and both builds passed, while four isolated Chromium profiles reproduced an admin cancellation button for IN_DELIVERY. Eight admin control checks and twelve customer browser checks passed. This is dated frontend evidence with mocked API boundaries, not backend/LDD verification. Current UI condition is web/admin/src/pages/Orders/OrderDetailDialog.tsx canCancel; PDD6.1 and test_admin_cannot_cancel_terminal_or_in_delivery prohibit the operation. Existing GRACE D1/D5 policy did not prevent a controller from stopping at source review until the user requested execution.

Alternatives.Alternative: More AGENTS.md MUST wording alone is insufficient: it cannot technically reject a result or block merge.
Local hooks alone are bypassable. Use a leaf local checker plus an independently protected CI acceptance boundary; do not claim either controls chat prose.
Prefer conservative whole-input fingerprints first. Dependency-aware reuse can reduce reruns later but risks accepting stale evidence and is outside the first increment.
Reuse existing test runners, GRACE MustPassCommand and verify.yml instead of replacing the methodology or implementing all deferred strict business E2E.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Implementation remains unauthorized. Future run/check command paths are explicit interfaces, not existing tools. Independent pytest subprocess tests validate the checker. Caps of120seconds for contract tests,30seconds for evidence checking and900seconds for narrow pilot execution are design acceptance limits; measure implementation against them later. Existing observations:84admin tests9.67seconds,75customer tests9.10seconds; browser admin75.352seconds and customer45.906seconds on the isolated reference host. Builds and installation are separate stages; these observations are not CI latency guarantees.

Read-only GitHub inspection on2026-11-09: repository public,default branch dev; traditional protection endpoint404, effective branch rules empty and rulesets empty. Available session permissions include admin. Thus no current remote enforcement exists. Before activation the human owner must approve the trust-base revision and configure protection with required checks/review and fresh candidate/base validation; ordinary agent credentials must lack settings/bypass rights. A session retaining owner/admin credentials cannot be claimed technically unable to disable policy. No permissions/settings were changed.

Trusted CI checker runs in an isolated aggregator job from the owner-approved protected base; candidate jobs are unprivileged producers. Never execute uploaded candidate scripts in the trusted job or deserialize executable formats. Workflow/checker/obligation/test-expectation changes require independent approval and update the trust base in a controlled stage; a PR cannot authorize its own weaker rules. Local evidence remains useful but not an authoritative remote attestation.

Bootstrap a trusted checker/policy before mandatory integration activation. Its own acceptance tests demonstrate both acceptance and rejection without certifying the currently failing product scenario.
Keep mandatory LDD/redaction and deferred broader business-gate requirements intact. A separate future change owns IN_DELIVERY UI repair; this tooling plan does not authorize it.
Rollback remains an explicitly authorized policy decision, never automatic warn-only fallback. Preserve failed artifacts and keep enforcement blocked while diagnosing verifier defects.

Scenarios.Scenario: Implementation: isolated collection and execution, evidence validation, outer GRACE final lint, authorized lifecycle closure, independent CI candidate check, then separately authorized protected merge.

Read-only review: bind claims and selected obligations to a source snapshot, execute required browser/backend checks, report partial if missing. Without a PR, only local tooling and controller reporting apply; remote enforcement cannot prevent an inaccurate chat response.
Archived history remains historical: enforce new lifecycle transitions relative to an adopted baseline, not every old applied bundle retroactively.

GraceChangeDesignContext.ExecutionAuthorization: User approved this plan and isolated gate implementation with negative checks. Business code, GitHub settings and commits remain out of scope. The approved plan's original proposal wording is retained as history; no approved assertion/scope/task was rewritten.
GraceChangeDesignContext.ExecutionBoundary: Local gate and CI preparation are distinct from remote activation. Current CI rejects first-closure transitions without prior approved CI evidence; transporting that evidence across commits is unresolved, not silently bypassed. Broader business/LDD automation remains deferred.

IndependentReviewDisposition.Outcome: Partial implementation; keep this bundle approved, not applied. Three independent sol 6.1 high reviewers inspected adapter behavior, CI trust and GRACE/plan compliance. Controller accepted the CI first-closure gap as an implementation blocker, not merely missing GitHub settings.
IndependentReviewDisposition.Corrections: Exact argv gate assertion, fixed excluded input boundaries, fresh browser builds, structural report redaction on failure, full browser identities, expected-failure/retry-aware Vitest reporting, runtime identities and fresh Python bytecode-cache namespace address concrete review findings. Negative checks must continue to reject rather than downgrade obligations.
IndependentReviewDisposition.OpenDecision: Prior approved CI closure authority must be separate from fresh current-run test evidence. A safe extension must verify trusted workflow/job provenance and normalized content/policy equality, reject expired/replayed/mixed evidence, and positively test first closure. No old context may be relabelled as fresh. Discuss this protocol before declaring the approved plan complete.
